items.summary: Background: Dental caries are chronic infectious diseases with a high global prevalence. items.title: The impact of periodontitis in cardiac autonomic dysfunction by hrv analysis.
items.authors: Vineetha S, Saravanan A, Jeyabanu M, et al.
items.summary: Introduction: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease damaging the supportive structure of teeth. It has systemic impacts including cardiac autonomic dysfunction. Heart Rate Variability (HRV) measures an objective analysis of the extent of autonomic regulation and where decreased parasympathetic activity coupled with increased sympathetic predominance was determined to correlate well with risk in cardiovascular events. This research ascertains periodontitis and its correlation to autonomic dysfunction by HRV analysis. items.authors: Ali S, Ayub SA, Ahmad S, et al.
items.summary: Background: Professionalism in dentistry extends beyond technical competence to include accountability, respect for patients and colleagues, non-maleficence, informed consent, communication, fairness, and conduct consistent with professional standards. Aim: To explore undergraduate dental students' experiences of, or observations of, events they perceived as unethical or inconsistent with professional conduct during clinical/workplace learning, and to understand the forms and meanings of these experiences. items.title: Cystathionine beta-synthase alleviates intervertebral disc degeneration by inhibiting ferroptosis of nucleus pulposus cells via the PI3K-AKT Axis.
items.authors: Yang CJ, Hu HF, Yang Y, et al.
items.summary: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is the leading cause of low back pain, affecting 619 million people worldwide in 2020, yet no effective disease-modifying therapy is clinically available to reverse its progression. Ferroptosis has been proven to be a core driver of IVDD by inducing injury to nucleus pulposus cells (NPCs). The regulatory role of cystathionine β-synthase (CBS) in IVDD and its underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the biological function of CBS in IVDD and elucidate the mechanism by which it regulates NPC ferroptosis. items.title: Autologous Conditioned Serum Improves Early Wound Healing Scores of Postextraction Dental Wound in Dogs.
items.authors: Šakarnytė L, Matsuzaki I, Troillet J, et al.
items.summary: This retrospective study evaluated the potential role of autologous conditioned serum (ACS) as an adjunctive therapy to improve postextraction dental wound healing in dogs. Clinical records of 40 dogs that underwent tooth extraction were included in the analysis. Data from 20 dogs that had received ACS applied to the extraction site following suturing were compared with those from 20 dogs that received the standard treatment. Healing outcomes were assessed from follow-up notes at days 3, 7 and 14, using the Early Wound Healing Score (EHS) to evaluate haemostasis, inflammation, and wound margin closure. items.title: Endodontic-Periodontal Lesions: Biological Basis, Diagnostic Challenges, and Contemporary Management Strategies.
items.authors: Mallya L, Roma M, Shetty K, et al.
items.summary: The dental pulp and periodontium are intimately connected through anatomical structures such as the apical foramen, lateral and accessory canals, and dentinal tubules, creating pathways for the bidirectional spread of infection and inflammation. This close relationship can result in endodontic-periodontal lesions, which often present significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to overlapping clinical and radiographic features. This review aims to examine the etiopathogenesis, classification, diagnostic considerations, and contemporary management approaches for endodontic-periodontal lesions.
